# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap/*

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related Projects

Augment clap:

- [wild](https://crates.io/crates/wild)for supporting wildcards (- `*`) on Windows like you do Linux
- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)
- [shadow-rs](https://crates.io/crates/shadow-rs)for generating- `Command::long_version`
- [clap_mangen](https://crates.io/crates/clap_mangen)for generating man page source (roff)
- [clap_complete](https://crates.io/crates/clap_complete)for shell completion support
- [clap-i18n-richformatter](https://crates.io/crates/clap-i18n-richformatter)for i18n support with- `clap::error::RichFormatter`

CLI Helpers

- [clio](https://crates.io/crates/clio)for reading/writing to files specified as arguments
- [clap-verbosity-flag](https://crates.io/crates/clap-verbosity-flag)

- [colorchoice-clap](https://crates.io/crates/colorchoice-clap)

Testing

- `snapbox`
- `assert_cmd`- `assert_fs`

# rustdoc_types - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/

## Expand description

Rustdoc’s JSON output interface

These types are the public API exposed through the `--output-format json` flag. The [ Crate](https://docs.rs/struct.Crate.html)
struct is the root of the JSON blob and all other items are contained within.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

[§](https://docs.rs#rustc-hash)`rustc-hash`

We expose a `rustc-hash` feature, disabled by default. This feature switches the
[ std::collections::HashMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/collections/hash/map/struct.HashMap.html) for [

`rustc_hash::FxHashMap`] to improve the performance of said
`HashMap` in specific situations.`cargo-semver-checks` for example, saw a [-3% improvement](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/266220-t-rustdoc/topic/rustc-hash.20and.20performance.20of.20rustdoc-types/near/474855731) when benchmarking using the
`aws_sdk_ec2` JSON output (~500MB of JSON). As always, we recommend measuring the impact before
turning this feature on, as [ FxHashMap](https://crates.io/crates/rustc-hash) only concerns itself with hash speed, and may
increase the number of collisions.

[§](https://docs.rs#rkyv_0_8)`rkyv_0_8`

We expose a `rkyv_0_8` feature, disabled by default. When enabled, it derives `rkyv`’s
[ Archive](https://docs.rs/rkyv/0.8.15/rkyv/trait.Archive.html),

[and](https://docs.rs/rkyv/0.8.15/rkyv/trait.Serialize.html)

`Serialize`[traits for all types in this crate. Furthermore, it exposes the corresponding](https://docs.rs/rkyv/0.8.15/rkyv/trait.Deserialize.html)

`Deserialize``Archived*` types (e.g. `ArchivedId` for [).](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html)

`Id``rkyv` lets you works with JSON output without paying the deserialization cost *upfront*,
thanks to [zero-copy deserialization](https://rkyv.org/zero-copy-deserialization.html).
You can perform various types of analyses on the `Archived*` version of the relevant types,
incurring the full deserialization cost only for the subset of items you actually need.

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# rustledger_ffi_wasi - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-ffi-wasi/0.19.1/rustledger_ffi_wasi/

## Expand description

Slimmed FFI-support helpers for the rustledger WASI component FFI.

[§](https://docs.rs#phase-5-1419-is-complete)Phase 5 (#1419) is complete

This crate used to expose a wasip1 JSON-RPC 2.0 embedding API (a server
binary in `main.rs` + a `jsonrpc` router) plus a `Directive → JSON` output
DTO. Both are gone: the JSON-RPC surface was retired earlier in Phase 5
([#1419](https://github.com/rustledger/rustledger/issues/1419)) now that the
typed WASI Preview 2 / Component Model binding,
[ rustledger-ffi-component](https://github.com/rustledger/rustledger/issues/1384)
(#1384), is the default embedding path (default in rustfava as of Phase 4);
the output DTO was removed once the component switched to converting
core→WIT directly.

What remains is a **library only** of FFI-support glue the component reuses:
the loader orchestration ([ helpers](https://docs.rs/helpers/index.html)), the WIT-input construction path
(

[+ the](https://docs.rs/fn.input_entry_to_directive.html)

`input_entry_to_directive``Input*` types) and directive hashing
([). These survivors are deliberately FFI glue kept OUT of the core](https://docs.rs/hash/fn.compute_directive_hash.html)

`compute_directive_hash``rustledger-loader` crate, so the crate is retained slimmed
rather than relocated or deleted (the “retained … document the decision”
outcome of #1419 item 6).## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use hash::`- [compute_directive_hash](https://docs.rs/hash/fn.compute_directive_hash.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- [Include](https://docs.rs/struct.Include.html)
- An include directive from the source file.
- [Input](https://docs.rs/struct.InputAmount.html)- Amount
- Input amount for entry creation.
- [Input](https://docs.rs/struct.InputCost.html)- Cost
- Input cost for entry creation.
- [Input](https://docs.rs/struct.InputPosting.html)- Posting
- Input posting for entry creation.
- [Ledger](https://docs.rs/struct.LedgerOptions.html)- Options
- [Plugin](https://docs.rs/struct.Plugin.html)
- A plugin directive from the source file.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Input](https://docs.rs/enum.InputCostNumber.html)- Cost - Number
- Input cost-number for entry creation.
- [Input](https://docs.rs/enum.InputEntry.html)- Entry
- Input entry for create-entry/format-entry commands.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [API_](https://docs.rs/constant.API_VERSION.html)- VERSION
- API version this server compiled against. Reported as the
`api_version`field on every method’s response (`util.version`,`ledger.load`, etc.).

# rustledger - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger/0.19.1/rustledger/

## Expand description

Beancount CLI tools.

This crate provides command-line tools for working with Beancount files:

- `rledger check`/- `bean-check`: Validate a beancount file
- `rledger format`/- `bean-format`: Format a beancount file
- `rledger query`/- `bean-query`: Query with BQL
- `rledger report`/- `bean-report`: Generate reports
- `rledger doctor`/- `bean-doctor`: Debugging tools

[§](https://docs.rs#example-usage)Example Usage

```
rledger check ledger.beancount
rledger format ledger.beancount
rledger query ledger.beancount "SELECT account, SUM(position)"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#related-crates)Related Crates

rustledger is a workspace with several crates:

| Crate | Description |
|---|---|
| `rustledger-core` | Core types (Amount, Position, Inventory, Directives) |
| `rustledger-parser` | Lexer and parser with error recovery |
| `rustledger-loader` | File loading, includes, options |
| `rustledger-booking` | Interpolation and booking engine |
| `rustledger-validate` | Validation with error reporting |
| `rustledger-query` | BQL query engine |
| `rustledger-plugin` | Native and WASM plugin system |
| `rustledger-wasm` | WebAssembly library target |
| `rustledger-importer` | Import framework for bank statements |
| `rustledger-lsp` | Language Server Protocol implementation |
| `rustledger-ffi-wasi` | FFI via WASI for embedding |

---

# rustledger_wasm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-wasm/0.19.1/rustledger_wasm/

## Expand description

Beancount WASM Bindings.

This crate provides WebAssembly bindings for using Beancount from JavaScript/TypeScript.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- Parse Beancount files (single and multi-file with includes)
- Validate ledgers
- Run BQL queries
- Format directives
- `ParsedLedger`
- `Ledger`

[§](https://docs.rs#example-javascript)Example (JavaScript)

```
import init, { parse, validateSource, query } from '@rustledger/wasm';
await init();
const source = `
2024-01-01 open Assets:Bank USD
2024-01-15 * "Coffee"
  Expenses:Food  5.00 USD
  Assets:Bank   -5.00 USD
`;
const result = parse(source);
if (result.errors.length === 0) {
    const validation = validateSource(source);
    console.log('Validation errors:', validation.errors);
}
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [convert](https://docs.rs/convert/index.html)
- Conversion functions between Beancount types and JSON DTOs.
- [types](https://docs.rs/types/index.html)
- Data transfer objects for WASM serialization.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Ledger](https://docs.rs/struct.Ledger.html)
- A fully processed multi-file ledger for queries and validation.
- [Parsed](https://docs.rs/struct.ParsedLedger.html)- Ledger
- A parsed and validated single-file ledger with editor features.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [balances](https://docs.rs/fn.balances.html)
- Calculate account balances.
- [bql_](https://docs.rs/fn.bql_completions.html)- completions
- Get BQL query completions at cursor position.
- [expand_](https://docs.rs/fn.expand_pads.html)- pads
- Process pad directives and expand them.
- [format](https://docs.rs/fn.format.html)
- Format a Beancount source string.
- [hash_](https://docs.rs/fn.hash_sources.html)- sources
- Compute a SHA-256 fingerprint of one or more source strings.
- [init](https://docs.rs/fn.init.html)
- Initialize the WASM module.
- [list_](https://docs.rs/fn.list_plugins.html)- plugins
- List available native plugins.
- [parse](https://docs.rs/fn.parse.html)
- Parse a Beancount source string.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_multi_file.html)- multi_ - file
- Parse multiple Beancount files with include resolution.
- [query](https://docs.rs/fn.query.html)
- Run a BQL query on a Beancount source string.
- [query_](https://docs.rs/fn.query_multi_file.html)- multi_ - file
- Run a BQL query on multiple Beancount files.
- [run_](https://docs.rs/fn.run_plugin.html)- plugin
- Run a single named plugin against a Beancount source and return the resulting directives as JSON.
- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_multi_file.html)- multi_ - file
- Validate multiple Beancount files with include resolution.

# rustledger_completion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-completion/0.19.1/rustledger_completion/

## Expand description

Editor-agnostic completion logic for Beancount sources.

This crate is the single source of truth for the completion logic
shared between the LSP (`rustledger-lsp`) and the WASM editor
(`rustledger-wasm`). It is deliberately pure: no clock access, no
`lsp-types`, no `wasm-bindgen`. Callers supply the live data
(account/currency/payee/tag/link string lists and “today’s” date)
and map the neutral [ CompletionCandidate](https://docs.rs/struct.CompletionCandidate.html) results into their own
editor-specific item types.

The two responsibilities are:

- **Context detection**—- `offset_to_byte`- `PositionEncoding`- `classify_context`- `CompletionContext`
- **Candidate generation**— the- `*_candidates`functions produce neutral- `CompletionCandidate`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Completion](https://docs.rs/struct.CompletionCandidate.html)- Candidate
- A neutral, editor-agnostic completion candidate.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Completion](https://docs.rs/enum.CompletionContext.html)- Context
- Completion context detected from cursor position.
- [Completion](https://docs.rs/enum.CompletionKind.html)- Kind
- The kind of a completion candidate.
- [Position](https://docs.rs/enum.PositionEncoding.html)- Encoding
- How a position offset is encoded by the caller.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [ACCOUNT_](https://docs.rs/constant.ACCOUNT_TYPES.html)- TYPES
- Standard Beancount account types.
- [DIRECTIVES](https://docs.rs/constant.DIRECTIVES.html)
- Standard Beancount directives.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [account_](https://docs.rs/fn.account_segment_candidates.html)- segment_ - candidates
- Candidates for the next account segment after a `prefix`.
- [account_](https://docs.rs/fn.account_start_candidates.html)- start_ - candidates
- Candidates when starting an account name: the standard account types followed by every known account.
- [after_](https://docs.rs/fn.after_date_candidates.html)- date_ - candidates
- Candidates after a date: the directive keywords.
- [classify_](https://docs.rs/fn.classify_context.html)- context
- Classify the completion context from the text before the cursor.
- [currency_](https://docs.rs/fn.currency_candidates.html)- candidates
- Candidates for a currency after an amount.
- [line_](https://docs.rs/fn.line_start_candidates.html)- start_ - candidates
- Candidates at line start: a single date template using the supplied
`today`string (the crate is clock-free; each adapter passes its own date).
- [link_](https://docs.rs/fn.link_candidates.html)- candidates
- Candidates for a link after `^`(issue #1268). Mirrors`tag_candidates``label`and dropped in`insert_text`.
- [offset_](https://docs.rs/fn.offset_to_byte.html)- to_ - byte
- Map a position `offset`(in the given`encoding`) into a byte offset into`line`, clamped to a char boundary.
- [payee_](https://docs.rs/fn.payee_candidates.html)- candidates
- Candidates for a payee/narration inside a string. Returns all known
payees — the client filters (issue #1183, the `.take(20)`trap).
- [tag_](https://docs.rs/fn.tag_candidates.html)- candidates
- Candidates for a tag after `#`(issue #1268).

# rustledger_importer - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-importer/0.19.1/rustledger_importer/

## Expand description

Import framework for rustledger

This crate provides the infrastructure for extracting transactions from bank statements, credit card statements, and other financial documents.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

The import system is modeled after Python beancount’s bean-extract. It uses
a trait-based approach where each importer implements the [ Importer](https://docs.rs/trait.Importer.html) trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use rustledger_importer::{ImporterConfig, ImporterRegistry};
use std::path::Path;
// Build the per-call config (CSV in this example).
let config = ImporterConfig::csv()
    .account("Assets:Bank:Checking")
    .date_column("Date")
    .narration_column("Description")
    .amount_column("Amount")
    .build()
    .unwrap();
// Dispatch through the registry — picks OfxImporter for .ofx/.qfx,
// CsvImporter for .csv. Returns an error for unknown extensions.
let registry = ImporterRegistry::with_builtins();
// let result = registry.extract(Path::new("bank.csv"), &config)?;
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use config::`- [ImporterConfig](https://docs.rs/config/struct.ImporterConfig.html);
- `pub use ofx_importer::`- [OfxImporter](https://docs.rs/ofx_importer/struct.OfxImporter.html);
- `pub use registry::`- [ImporterRegistry](https://docs.rs/registry/struct.ImporterRegistry.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [config](https://docs.rs/config/index.html)
- Configuration for importers.
- [csv_](https://docs.rs/csv_importer/index.html)- importer
- CSV file importer.
- [csv_](https://docs.rs/csv_inference/index.html)- inference
- CSV format auto-inference.
- [ofx_](https://docs.rs/ofx_importer/index.html)- importer
- OFX/QFX file importer.
- [registry](https://docs.rs/registry/index.html)
- Registry for importers.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Enriched](https://docs.rs/struct.EnrichedImportResult.html)- Import - Result
- Result of an enriched import operation.
- [Import](https://docs.rs/struct.ImportResult.html)- Result
- Result of an import operation.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Importer](https://docs.rs/trait.Importer.html)
- Trait for file importers.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- Auto-extract transactions from a file by inferring its format.

# rustledger_query - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-query/0.19.1/rustledger_query/

## Expand description

Beancount Query Language (BQL) engine.

This crate provides a SQL-like query language for analyzing Beancount ledger data.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

BQL is a specialized query language designed for financial data analysis. It operates on transaction postings while respecting double-entry bookkeeping constraints.

[§](https://docs.rs#query-types)Query Types

- `SELECT`- General purpose queries with filtering, grouping, and ordering
- `JOURNAL`- Shorthand for account statements
- `BALANCES`- Shorthand for account balance tables
- `PRINT`- Output filtered transactions in Beancount syntax

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use rustledger_query::parse;
let query = parse("SELECT account, SUM(position) WHERE account ~ \"Expenses:\" GROUP BY account").unwrap();
println!("{:?}", query);
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use error::`- [ParseError](https://docs.rs/error/struct.ParseError.html);
- `pub use error::`- [QueryError](https://docs.rs/error/enum.QueryError.html);
- `pub use executor::`- [Executor](https://docs.rs/executor/struct.Executor.html);
- `pub use executor::`- [Interval](https://docs.rs/executor/struct.Interval.html);
- `pub use executor::`- [IntervalUnit](https://docs.rs/executor/enum.IntervalUnit.html);

- `pub use executor::`- [Value](https://docs.rs/executor/enum.Value.html);

- `pub use price::`- [PriceDatabase](https://docs.rs/price/struct.PriceDatabase.html);

# noesis_bevy - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/noesis_bevy/0.12.1/noesis_bevy/

## Expand description

Bevy plugin for the Noesis GUI SDK.

Drives `libNoesis.so` through the [ noesis_runtime](https://docs.rs/noesis_runtime/0.12.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/noesis_runtime/index.html) FFI crate and implements

`Noesis::RenderDevice` on top of Bevy’s wgpu device. UIs render into an
offscreen wgpu texture and composite into the Bevy frame.Add [ NoesisPlugin](https://docs.rs/struct.NoesisPlugin.html) to initialize the runtime, then host XAML through a

[camera.](https://docs.rs/render/struct.NoesisView.html)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [animation](https://docs.rs/animation/index.html)
- Per-view code-built property animations: the runtime-driven counterpart to a
XAML `<Storyboard>`/`<DoubleAnimation>`declared inline in a`ControlTemplate`or`Style.Triggers`.
- [bake](https://docs.rs/bake/index.html)
- Bake an XAML view to an offscreen `Handle<Image>`
- [binding](https://docs.rs/binding/index.html)
- Per-view value-converter / multi-binding bridge: install a code-built
`{Binding}`, driven by a**Rust**`ValueConverter``MultiValueConverter`
- [brushes](https://docs.rs/brushes/index.html)
- Per-view code-built brush bridge: paint named XAML elements with brushes
constructed in Rust, no XAML authoring required. The brush counterpart of the
`crate::dp``crate::geometry`
- [classes](https://docs.rs/classes/index.html)
- Register Rust-backed XAML classes (`<myns:Foo>`) with Noesis from Bevy systems.
- [commands](https://docs.rs/commands/index.html)
- Per-view Rust-owned `ICommand`bridge.
- [diagnostics](https://docs.rs/diagnostics/index.html)
- App-level diagnostics bridge: surface Noesis’s process-global allocator counters as a Bevy resource and route its error handler into Bevy’s log.
- [dp](https://docs.rs/dp/index.html)
- Per-view generic dependency-property get/set bridge, keyed by
`(x:Name, property)`.
- [events](https://docs.rs/events/index.html)
- Per-view routed-event bridge: surface `BaseButton::Click`and`UIElement::KeyDown`from named elements of a single`crate::NoesisView`**and**Bevy`EntityEvent`s (observers).
- [focus](https://docs.rs/focus/index.html)
- Per-view keyboard-focus bridge: give a named XAML element keyboard
focus on a single `crate::NoesisView`
- [focus_](https://docs.rs/focus_input/index.html)- input
- Per-view focus-navigation and input-binding bridge: the directional,
engagement, and key-chord layer on top of the one-shot `crate::NoesisFocus`
- [font](https://docs.rs/font/index.html)
- Font-asset plumbing for the Bevy plugin.
- [geometry](https://docs.rs/geometry/index.html)
- Per-view geometry bridge: imperative vector polyline writes against named
XAML `Path`elements on a single`NoesisView``crate::text`
- [headless](https://docs.rs/headless/index.html)
- Headless harness entry point for tests and CI.
- [image](https://docs.rs/image/index.html)
- Image-asset plumbing for the `ImageBrush`/`Image`loader.
- [imaging](https://docs.rs/imaging/index.html)
- Per-view code-built imaging bridge: drive a named `<Image>`’s pixels from a Rust-provided bitmap (RGBA8 + size), no image file on disk required. The imaging counterpart of the`crate::brushes``crate::geometry`
- [inlines](https://docs.rs/inlines/index.html)
- Per-view **formatted text**bridge: give a named`TextBlock`rich inline content (`Run`/`Bold`/`Italic`/`Underline`/`Span`/`Hyperlink`/`LineBreak`) from Bevy, then read the resulting live structure back.
- [input](https://docs.rs/input/index.html)
- Bevy → Noesis input forwarding.
- [integration](https://docs.rs/integration/index.html)
- App-level system-integration bridge.
- [items](https://docs.rs/items/index.html)
- Per-view `ItemsSource`bridge: populate XAML list controls (`ComboBox`/`ListBox`/`ItemsControl`) from a Bevy app, with typed items.
- [layout](https://docs.rs/layout/index.html)
- Per-view `Margin`writes against named XAML elements: the positioning primitive for floating panels (context menus, popups, tooltips) that must follow gameplay coordinates.
- [list](https://docs.rs/list/index.html)
- **Primitive 2: list = query.**The rows of a XAML list control- *are*Bevy entities: spawn an entity carrying a row-data component and a- `ListedIn`- `ObservableCollection`is reconciled from the query keyed by- `Entity`- **minimal**Add / Remove / Update / Move op sequence (never a- `Clear`/- `Reset`in steady state), so a control’s selection and scroll position survive every edit.
- [markup](https://docs.rs/markup/index.html)
- Custom `MarkupExtension`registration for Bevy.
- [panel](https://docs.rs/panel/index.html)
- **Primitive 1: panel = entity.**A- `UiPanel`- `NoesisView`- *bound components*on that same entity- **are**its- `DataContext`.
- [plain_](https://docs.rs/plain_vm/index.html)- vm
- Per-view plain-struct `ViewModel`bridge: bind a plain Bevy`Component`to a view’s XAML`{Binding field_name}`by field name, two-way.
- [reconcile](https://docs.rs/reconcile/index.html)
- “Diff in parallel, push serially”: the reconcile convention the data-driven bridges (list reconcile, panel/DataContext reconcile) are built on.
- [render](https://docs.rs/render/index.html)
- Render integration: drives each `NoesisView`
- [render_](https://docs.rs/render_device/index.html)- device
- wgpu-backed render device for Noesis. This module pulls in no Bevy types, so you can drive it with a hand-built wgpu instance in tests.
- [resources](https://docs.rs/resources/index.html)
- App-level application-resources bridge. Registers Rust-built resources
(code-built brushes, scalar values) and merged `<ResourceDictionary>`XAML into the process-global application resources, so XAML`{StaticResource Key}`references resolve them without authoring a theme file on disk.
- [routed_](https://docs.rs/routed_events/index.html)- events
- Per-view **generic routed-event**bridge: surface any`RoutedEvent`(mouse, key, focus, drag, manipulation, lifecycle bubbling, …) from named elements of a single`crate::NoesisView`
- [shapes](https://docs.rs/shapes/index.html)
- Per-view shapes bridge: build a Noesis vector `Shape`(`Rectangle`,`Ellipse`, or`Line`) entirely in Rust and assign it as the content of a named XAML container element on a single`NoesisView`
- [styles](https://docs.rs/styles/index.html)
- Per-view code-built `Style`bridge: restyle named XAML elements with a`Noesis::Style`constructed in Rust, no XAML authoring required. The style counterpart of the`crate::dp``crate::brushes`
- [svg](https://docs.rs/svg/index.html)
- Per-view SVG bridge: drive a named XAML element from an SVG *path-data*source string parsed in Rust. The SVG counterpart of the`crate::geometry`
- [text](https://docs.rs/text/index.html)
- Per-view `Text`bridge: write and observe the`Text`of named XAML elements (`TextBox`/`TextBlock`) on a single`crate::NoesisView`
- [theme](https://docs.rs/theme/index.html)
- Opt-in loader for Noesis’s shipped control theme.
- [transforms](https://docs.rs/transforms/index.html)
- Per-view `RenderTransform`writes against named XAML elements: the post-layout scale / skew / rotate / translate that drives UI motion (a button that pops on hover, a panel that slides in, a spinning loader) without touching layout.
- [transforms3d](https://docs.rs/transforms3d/index.html)
- Per-view **3D transform**writes against named XAML elements: the`UIElement.Transform3D`attached behaviour (WinUI/Noesis) that rotates, scales and translates an element in 3D space about a center, with the implicit projection camera supplying perspective. Distinct from the 2D`RenderTransform`bridge (`crate::transforms``RenderTransform`, this one sets`Transform3D`.
- [typography](https://docs.rs/typography/index.html)
- Per-view typography bridge: restyle the `TextElement`font properties (size, family, weight, style, stretch) of named XAML elements on a single`NoesisView`
- [ui](https://docs.rs/ui/index.html)
- `NoesisUi`- `NoesisView`
- [viewmodel](https://docs.rs/viewmodel/index.html)
- Per-view Rust-owned `ViewModel`/`DataContext`bridge.
- [visibility](https://docs.rs/visibility/index.html)
- Per-view visibility bridge: show or hide named XAML elements on a single
`NoesisView`
- [visual_](https://docs.rs/visual_state/index.html)- state
- Per-view `VisualStateManager::GoToState`writes against named XAML controls: the code-driven counterpart to a`ControlTemplate`’s trigger-driven visual states (e.g. a control’s`CommonStates`:`Normal`/`MouseOver`/`Pressed`/`Disabled`, or app-authored groups).
- [window_](https://docs.rs/window_compat/index.html)- compat
- `Window`root-element compatibility shim.
- [xaml](https://docs.rs/xaml/index.html)
- XAML asset plumbing: feeds Bevy-loaded XAML bytes to Noesis’s parser.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Convert](https://docs.rs/struct.ConvertArg.html)- Arg
- A borrowed, boxed binding value handed to a `ValueConverter``None`-valued (the bound source produced null / the control supplied no parameter) reports`is_none``None`when the boxed runtime type doesn’t match.
- [Modifier](https://docs.rs/struct.ModifierKeys.html)- Keys
- A typed bitset of `Noesis::ModifierKeys`: the chord modifiers held down (`Alt`/`Control`/`Shift`/`Windows`). Compose with`Self::with``FromIterator``Self::contains`
- [Noesis](https://docs.rs/struct.NoesisLicense.html)- License
- Per-developer Indie license credentials.
- [Noesis](https://docs.rs/struct.NoesisPlugin.html)- Plugin
- Bevy plugin that initializes Noesis at app startup and shuts it down when
the `App`
- [Plain](https://docs.rs/struct.PlainValueRef.html)- Value - Ref
- A borrowed, boxed value handed to a `PlainSetHandler``TwoWay`writeback). The typed accessors return`None`when the boxed runtime type doesn’t match / the value is null.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Binding](https://docs.rs/enum.BindingMode.html)- Mode
- How a `Binding``Noesis::BindingMode`.
- [Converted](https://docs.rs/enum.Converted.html)
- A value a `ValueConverter``Noesis::BaseComponent*`the binding engine expects.
- [Cursor](https://docs.rs/enum.CursorType.html)- Type
- Built-in cursor kind Noesis asks the host to display. Re-exported from the
runtime so consumers can match on `NoesisCursorRequested::cursor``noesis_runtime`directly. Built-in cursor types, mirroring`Noesis::CursorType`in`NsGui/Cursor.h`. The discriminants match the C++ enum exactly so the value read back from a live`Cursor`round-trips.
- [Focus](https://docs.rs/enum.FocusNavigationDirection.html)- Navigation - Direction
- Mirror of `Noesis::FocusNavigationDirection`: the direction for`FrameworkElement::move_focus``FrameworkElement::predict_focus``Next`/`Previous`/`First`/`Last`are tab-order traversal (not supported by`predict_focus`), while`Left`/`Right`/`Up`/`Down`are directional.
- [Font](https://docs.rs/enum.FontStretch.html)- Stretch
- `Noesis::FontStretch`.
- [Font](https://docs.rs/enum.FontStyle.html)- Style
- `Noesis::FontStyle`.
- [Font](https://docs.rs/enum.FontWeight.html)- Weight
- `Noesis::FontWeight`. The numeric value- *is*the weight (e.g.- `Normal`= 400,- `Bold`= 700), matching the OpenType- `usWeightClass`.
- [Key](https://docs.rs/enum.Key.html)
- Common subset of `Noesis::Key`from`NsGui/InputEnums.h`. Values are the C++ enum ordinals, validated by`static_assert`in`noesis_view.cpp`.`View::key_down`
- [Mouse](https://docs.rs/enum.MouseButton.html)- Button
- Mirror of `Noesis::MouseButton`from`NsGui/InputEnums.h`. Ordinals validated at C++ compile time via`static_assert`in`noesis_view.cpp`.
- [Plain](https://docs.rs/enum.PlainType.html)- Type
- Content type of a reflected plain-VM property. Mirrors `noesis_plain_type`in`cpp/noesis_shim.h`; the ordinal is the FFI tag.
- [Plain](https://docs.rs/enum.PlainValue.html)- Value
- A value to push into a plain-VM property. The crate boxes it into the
`BaseComponent*`the binding engine reads.
- [Routed](https://docs.rs/enum.RoutedEvent.html)- Event
- A documented `Noesis::RoutedEvent`accepted by`subscribe_event``noesis_events.cpp`), so the typed accessors on`EventArgs``subscribe_event_by_name`
- [Text](https://docs.rs/enum.TextDecorations.html)- Decorations
- Re-exported from `noesis_runtime`: the`TextDecorations`an inline can carry (see`InlineSpec::decorated``TextDecorations`an`Inline``Noesis::TextDecorations`.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Multi](https://docs.rs/trait.MultiValueConverter.html)- Value - Converter
- Rust-side multi-value conversion logic: combine the source values of the
child bindings into one target value. Returning `None`signals`UnsetValue`(the binding falls back to its`FallbackValue`/ the property default).
- [Value](https://docs.rs/trait.ValueConverter.html)- Converter
- Rust-side conversion logic. `convert`maps a binding source value to the target;`convert_back`(only reached on a`TwoWay`/`OneWayToSource`binding) maps a target value back to the source. Returning`None`signals`UnsetValue`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_culture.html)- culture
- Return the active default culture’s BCP-47 name. Defaults to `"en-US"`before any`set_culture`
- [open_](https://docs.rs/fn.open_url.html)- url
- Ask Noesis to open `url`. Invokes the registered open-URL callback synchronously; a no-op if none is registered.
- [play_](https://docs.rs/fn.play_audio.html)- audio
- Ask Noesis to play the sound at `uri`at`volume`. Invokes the registered play-audio callback synchronously; a no-op if none is registered.
- [set_](https://docs.rs/fn.set_culture.html)- culture
- Set the default culture by BCP-47 name (e.g. `"en-US"`,`"fr-FR"`). The name backs Noesis’s number / currency / date formatting. Round-trips through`get_culture`

## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [Noesis](https://docs.rs/derive.NoesisViewModel.html)- View - Model
- Derive macro for `NoesisViewModel`

For example, a call to
xMessageBufferCreate() returns an MessageBufferHandle_t variable that can
then be used as a parameter to xMessageBufferSend(), xMessageBufferReceive(),
etc. Message buffer is essentially built as a stream buffer hence its handle
is also set to same type as a stream buffer handle. MiniListItem_t    PendedFunction_t   QueueHandle_t   QueueSetHandle_t   Type by which queue sets are referenced.  For example, a call to
xQueueCreateSet() returns an xQueueSet variable that can then be used as a
parameter to xQueueSelectFromSet(), xQueueAddToSet(), etc. QueueSetMemberHandle_t    Queue sets can contain both queues and semaphores, so the
QueueSetMemberHandle_t is defined as a type to be used where a parameter or
return value can be either an QueueHandle_t or an SemaphoreHandle_t. # rustledger_plugin - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-plugin/0.19.1/rustledger_plugin/

## Expand description

Beancount WASM Plugin Runtime.

This crate provides a plugin system for extending Beancount’s functionality. Plugins can be written in any language that compiles to WebAssembly, or as native Rust code for maximum performance.

[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

The plugin system uses wasmtime as the WASM runtime with `MessagePack`
serialization for passing data across the WASM boundary.

[§](https://docs.rs#plugin-types)Plugin Types

- **WASM Plugins**: Sandboxed plugins loaded from- `.wasm`files
- **Native Plugins**: Built-in plugins implemented in Rust

[§](https://docs.rs#built-in-plugins-31)Built-in Plugins (31)

See the [plugin reference](https://rustledger.github.io/docs/reference/plugins) for the full list.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use rustledger_plugin::{PluginManager, PluginInput, PluginOptions};
let mut manager = PluginManager::new();
manager.load(Path::new("my_plugin.wasm"))?;
let input = PluginInput {
    directives: vec![],
    options: PluginOptions::default(),
    config: None,
};
let output = manager.execute_all(input)?;
```

# rustledger_loader - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-loader/0.19.1/rustledger_loader/

## Expand description

Beancount file loader with include resolution.

This crate handles loading beancount files, resolving includes, and collecting options. It builds on the parser to provide a complete loading pipeline.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- Recursive include resolution with cycle detection
- Options collection and parsing
- Plugin directive collection
- Source map for error reporting
- Push/pop tag and metadata handling
- Automatic GPG decryption for encrypted files (`.gpg`,`.asc`)

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

# postings - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/postings/0.2.0/postings/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#postings)postings

A small inverted-index core built around postings lists.

[§](https://docs.rs#scope-deliberate)Scope (deliberate)

- This crate is **index-only**: it does not store document content.
- It supports **candidate generation**with**no false negatives**(a caller may choose to verify candidates with an exact matcher).
- It uses a Lucene-style mental model: immutable “segments” (here: append-only batches) and logical deletes.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-modules)Optional modules

- `postings::codec`: low-level codecs (varint/gap) for postings payloads (in this repo).
- `postings::positional`(feature- `positional`): positional postings for phrase/proximity evaluation.
- `postings::raw`(feature- `raw-segment`): byte- and file-backed raw segment reader experiments.

[§](https://docs.rs#non-goals-for-now)Non-goals (for now)

- Full on-disk compaction
- Rich query language beyond candidate generation and sparse top-k scoring

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [codec](https://docs.rs/codec/index.html)
- Low-level codecs and iterator contracts for postings payloads.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Planner](https://docs.rs/struct.PlannerConfig.html)- Config
- Configuration for candidate planning / bailout.
- [Postings](https://docs.rs/struct.PostingsIndex.html)- Index
- A postings-based inverted index with segment-style updates.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Candidate](https://docs.rs/enum.CandidatePlan.html)- Plan
- Planner output for candidate generation.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Errors returned by `postings`.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Weight](https://docs.rs/trait.Weight.html)
- Trait for term weight types in posting lists.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- Document identifier.

# rustledger_validate - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rustledger-validate/0.19.1/rustledger_validate/

## Expand description

Beancount validation rules.

This crate implements validation checks for beancount ledgers:

- Account lifecycle (opened before use, not used after close)
- Balance assertions
- Transaction balancing
- Currency constraints
- Booking validation (lot matching, sufficient units)

[§](https://docs.rs#error-codes)Error Codes

All error codes follow the spec in `spec/core/validation.md`:

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| E1001 | Account not opened |
| E1002 | Account already open |
| E1003 | Account already closed |
| E1004 | Account close with non-zero balance |
| E1005 | Invalid account name |
| E2001 | Balance assertion failed |
| E2002 | Balance exceeds explicit tolerance |
| E2003 | Pad without subsequent balance |
| E2004 | Multiple pads for same balance |
| E3001 | Transaction does not balance |
| E3002 | Multiple missing amounts in transaction |
| E3003 | Transaction has no postings |
| E3004 | Transaction has single posting (warning) |
| E4001 | No matching lot for reduction |
| E4002 | Insufficient units in lot |
| E4003 | Ambiguous lot match |
| E4005 | Negative cost amount |
| E5001 | Currency not declared |
| E5002 | Currency not allowed in account |
| E5003 | Invalid `precision`metadata on commodity directive (warning) |
| E7001 | Unknown option |
| E7002 | Invalid option value |
| E7003 | Duplicate option |
| E8001 | Document file not found |
| E10001 | Date out of order (info) |
| E10002 | Entry dated in the future (warning) |

# sim_codec - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-codec/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Core decoder/encoder and output-position contracts for the SIM codec layer.

sim-codec is the foundation crate of the sim-codec-* family. The SIM kernel
defines the `Expr` graph and the codec contract types; this crate provides
the concrete runtime that every other codec crate implements against: the
`Decoder`/`Encoder` traits, their located and tree-shaped variants, the
`DecodePosition`/`DecodeTarget` output-position model (eval, quote, data,
pattern), and the `CodecRuntime` glue that registers a codec as a
runtime object. On top of those contracts it carries the shared
`Expr`<->tree encode machinery, domain-codec scaffolding, decode resource
limits, portable encode/decode, string-literal coding, and tree validation.

A decoder turns tokens or text into a checked `Expr` form; an encoder knows
its output position and renders an `Expr` back to text or bytes. Downstream
crates (general-purpose and domain codecs) build on these primitives rather
than re-implementing them.

Module map (these modules are private; their public items are re-exported at the crate root, so they are listed here in plain text rather than linked):

- implementation: implementation root that aggregates the submodules below
and re-exports their public surface.
- runtime: the `Decoder`/`Encoder`runtime contracts, the`DecodePosition`/`DecodeTarget`output positions,`Input`/`Output`, and the`CodecRuntime`registration glue.
- domain: builder scaffolding for domain codec libs (`DomainCodecLib`) and the shared UTF-8 input helper.
- domain_form: a generic `#(...)`domain-form parser and formatter.
- limits: decode resource ceilings (`DecodeLimits`), running budgets (`DecodeBudget`), and the`ReadCx`decode context.
- list_encode: the shared list/`Expr`value-to-expr encode machinery.
- portable: codec-neutral, lossless portable encode/decode for the data
subset of `Expr`.
- strings: string-literal encode/decode helpers.
- tree: structural validation of a `LocatedExprTree`.

- runtime: the
- runtime_api: the eval-facing surface that drives codecs through the kernel
(`DecodedForm`, codec lookup, and decode/encode entry points).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Codec](https://docs.rs/struct.CodecRuntime.html)- Runtime
- A registered codec as a runtime object: a symbol-named bundle of optional decode/encode capabilities plus the Shapes and default-decode policy it exposes.
- [Decode](https://docs.rs/struct.DecodeBudget.html)- Budget
- Running counters for a single decode. Construct one per decode call.
- [Decode](https://docs.rs/struct.DecodeLimits.html)- Limits
- Resource ceiling shared by every codec decode path.
- [Domain](https://docs.rs/struct.DomainCodecLib.html)- Codec - Lib
- A host-registered lib that exports one codec (and optionally the Shapes it uses) built from a decoder and encoder.
- [Domain](https://docs.rs/struct.DomainForm.html)- Form
- A parsed `#(name ...)`form: a name, keyed fields, and positional values.
- [Loss](https://docs.rs/struct.LossReport.html)- Report
- Loss report for one parse/encode/reparse cycle.
- [Prism](https://docs.rs/struct.PrismDiagnostic.html)- Diagnostic
- A parse diagnostic surfaced by the Prism.
- [Prism](https://docs.rs/struct.PrismEncode.html)- Encode
- Encode result for one codec surface.
- [Prism](https://docs.rs/struct.PrismInspection.html)- Inspection
- Metadata describing how input was inspected.
- [Prism](https://docs.rs/struct.PrismParse.html)- Parse
- Parse result for one codec surface.
- [Prism](https://docs.rs/struct.PrismSpan.html)- Span
- A half-open byte span belonging to a parsed surface.
- [ReadCx](https://docs.rs/struct.ReadCx.html)
- The decode context threaded through every `Decoder`
- [Round](https://docs.rs/struct.RoundTrip.html)- Trip
- Full round-trip proof for one codec surface.
- [Runtime](https://docs.rs/struct.RuntimeCodecPrism.html)- Codec - Prism
- Runtime-backed `CodecPrism`
- [Semantic](https://docs.rs/struct.SemanticId.html)- Id
- Stable identity for a semantic expression.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Binary](https://docs.rs/enum.BinaryCarrier.html)- Carrier
- How binary frame bytes are carried at the codec boundary.
- [Codec](https://docs.rs/enum.CodecDefaultDecode.html)- Default - Decode
- A codec’s policy for choosing a `DecodeTarget``DecodePosition`
- [Decode](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodePosition.html)- Position
- The syntactic position a decode is targeting, mirroring the kernel’s
`EncodePosition`.
- [Decode](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodeTarget.html)- Target
- The checked form a decode resolves to once a position is known: inert data or an evaluable term.
- [Decoded](https://docs.rs/enum.DecodedForm.html)- Form
- The position-resolved result of a default decode: inert data or an evaluable term.
- [Diagnostic](https://docs.rs/enum.DiagnosticSeverity.html)- Severity
- Diagnostic severity.
- [Domain](https://docs.rs/enum.DomainFormError.html)- Form - Error
- A domain-form parse or access error.
- [Domain](https://docs.rs/enum.DomainValue.html)- Value
- A parsed domain-form value.
- [Input](https://docs.rs/enum.Input.html)
- Raw input handed to a `Decoder`
- [Output](https://docs.rs/enum.Output.html)
- Rendered output produced by an `Encoder`
- [Prism](https://docs.rs/enum.PrismInputKind.html)- Input - Kind
- What kind of input the Prism inspected.
- [Prism](https://docs.rs/enum.PrismOutput.html)- Output
- Output from a Prism encode pass.
- [Prism](https://docs.rs/enum.PrismSurface.html)- Surface
- The class of codec surface a Prism is driving.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Codec](https://docs.rs/trait.CodecPrism.html)- Prism
- A codec-aware editor contract for one codec surface.
- [Decoder](https://docs.rs/trait.Decoder.html)
- The core decode contract: turn `Input``Expr`.
- [Encoder](https://docs.rs/trait.Encoder.html)
- The core encode contract: render a kernel `Expr`to`Output`
- [Located](https://docs.rs/trait.LocatedDecoder.html)- Decoder
- A decoder that preserves source `Origin`, producing a`LocatedExpr`
- [Located](https://docs.rs/trait.LocatedEncoder.html)- Encoder
- An encoder that consumes a `LocatedExpr``Encoder`
- [Tree](https://docs.rs/trait.TreeDecoder.html)- Decoder
- A decoder that preserves the full source tree as a `LocatedExprTree`
- [Tree](https://docs.rs/trait.TreeEncoder.html)- Encoder
- An encoder that consumes a full `LocatedExprTree`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [codec_](https://docs.rs/fn.codec_value.html)- value
- Wrap a `CodecRuntime``Value`
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_datum_with_codec.html)- datum_ - with_ - codec
- Decode `input`to a`Datum`with the codec named`symbol`, using default`DecodeLimits`
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_datum_with_codec_and_limits.html)- datum_ - with_ - codec_ - and_ - limits
- Decode `input`to a`Datum`under explicit`DecodeLimits``Expr`is not inert data.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_default_with_codec.html)- default_ - with_ - codec
- Decode `input`and resolve it to data or a term per the codec’s policy and the requested`position`, using default`DecodeLimits`
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_default_with_codec_and_limits.html)- default_ - with_ - codec_ - and_ - limits
- Position-aware decode under explicit `DecodeLimits``decode_default_with_codec`
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_located_with_codec.html)- located_ - with_ - codec
- Decode `input`preserving source origin, attributing spans to`source_id`, using default`DecodeLimits`
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_located_with_codec_and_limits.html)- located_ - with_ - codec_ - and_ - limits
- Origin-preserving decode under explicit `DecodeLimits``decode_located_with_codec`
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_portable.html)- portable
- Parse codec-neutral portable text back into an `Expr`, failing closed on any malformed input rather than panicking.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_string_literal.html)- string_ - literal
- Parse a double-quoted, escaped string literal back to its value.
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_term_with_codec.html)- term_ - with_ - codec
- Decode `input`to an evaluable`Term`with the codec named`symbol`, using default`DecodeLimits`
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_term_with_codec_and_limits.html)- term_ - with_ - codec_ - and_ - limits
- Decode `input`to a`Term`under explicit`DecodeLimits``Expr`to a term per the codec’s`CodecDefaultDecode`
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_tree_with_codec.html)- tree_ - with_ - codec
- Decode `input`into a full`LocatedExprTree``source_id`, using default`DecodeLimits`
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_tree_with_codec_and_limits.html)- tree_ - with_ - codec_ - and_ - limits
- Full-tree decode under explicit `DecodeLimits``decode_tree_with_codec`
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_with_codec.html)- with_ - codec
- Decode `input`with the codec named`symbol`, using default`DecodeLimits`
- [decode_](https://docs.rs/fn.decode_with_codec_and_limits.html)- with_ - codec_ - and_ - limits
- Decode `input`with the codec named`symbol`under explicit`DecodeLimits`
- [domain_](https://docs.rs/fn.domain_input_text.html)- input_ - text
- Read a codec `Input`as UTF-8 text, tagging any error with`codec`. The shared body of every domain codec’s`input_text`helper.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_datum_with_codec.html)- datum_ - with_ - codec
- Encode a `Datum`with the codec named`symbol`, lifting it to an`Expr`first.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_located_with_codec.html)- located_ - with_ - codec
- Encode a `LocatedExpr``symbol`, using its origin for fidelity when`options`request lossless-origin output.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_portable.html)- portable
- Serialize a data-subset `Expr`into the codec-neutral portable text form.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_string_literal.html)- string_ - literal
- Render `value`as a double-quoted, backslash-escaped string literal.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_term_with_codec.html)- term_ - with_ - codec
- Encode a `Term`with the codec named`symbol`, lifting it to an`Expr`first.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_tree_with_codec.html)- tree_ - with_ - codec
- Encode a `LocatedExprTree``symbol`, reproducing layout and trivia when`options`request lossless-origin output.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_value_expr.html)- value_ - expr
- Walk a runtime `Value`into a kernel`Expr`ready for encoding.
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_value_with_codec.html)- value_ - with_ - codec
- Encode a runtime `Value`with the codec named`symbol`, forcing lists and tables into an`Expr`via`encode_value_expr`
- [encode_](https://docs.rs/fn.encode_with_codec.html)- with_ - codec
- Encode `expr`with the codec named`symbol`under`options`.
- [force_](https://docs.rs/fn.force_list_for_encode.html)- list_ - for_ - encode
- Force a list value into a bounded Vec for v1 encoding.
- [format_](https://docs.rs/fn.format_domain_form.html)- domain_ - form
- Render a domain form as an ASCII `#(...)`string. Round-trips through`parse_domain_form`
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_domain_form.html)- domain_ - form
- Parse a top-level `#(...)`domain form.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_expr_shape.html)- expr_ - shape
- Resolve a general codec’s expression shape: the `primary`symbol, then`core/Expr`, then`core/Any`, then nil. This is the shared fallback chain that every general-purpose codec (json/binary/binary-base64/algol/lisp/doc) hand-rolled identically before OVERLAP6.07.
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_options_shape.html)- options_ - shape
- Resolve a general codec’s encode-options shape: `core/EncodeOptions`, then`core/Any`, then nil. The shared fallback chain those codecs hand-rolled.
- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_expr_tree.html)- expr_ - tree
- Check that a `LocatedExprTree``Expr`.

---

# sim_kernel - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

sim-kernel is the small protocol kernel of the SIM Rust runtime.

The kernel defines contracts; libraries supply behavior. This crate holds
the protocol and contract types – forms, values, stores, registry and
callable surfaces, the [ shape](https://docs.rs/shape/index.html) protocol, evaluation policy, and the ABI
transport – while concrete behavior (parsers, number domains, the standard
distribution, and server/agent/browse implementations) lives in separate
library crates loaded against these contracts. SIM is a Rust runtime, not a
Lisp runtime; Lisp is one codec surface among several.

The one deliberate exception is the pair of built-in *reference backends*:
[ list::VecList](https://docs.rs/list/struct.VecList.html) (a

[) and](https://docs.rs/list/trait.ListValue.html)

`list::ListValue`[(a](https://docs.rs/table/struct.AssocTable.html)

`table::AssocTable`[). These are the kernel’s bootstrap list and table implementations – minimal, correct, and self-annotated](https://docs.rs/table/trait.Table.html)

`table::Table``sim-non-citizen` –
so the runtime can stand up collections before any library loads. They are
reference implementations, not the only backends: alternatives load as libs
against the [/](https://docs.rs/list/trait.ListBackend.html)

`list::ListBackend`[contracts. (Future cleanup: move even these into a default-loaded distribution lib so the kernel ships pure contracts; tracked against the constellation reorg.)](https://docs.rs/table/trait.TableBackend.html)

`table::TableBackend`The kernel data flow is:

`tokens -> checked forms -> objects -> checked calls -> objects -> encoded forms`[§](https://docs.rs#module-map)Module map

Core forms and values: [ value](https://docs.rs/value/index.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/expr/index.html)

# sim_lib_control - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-control/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Control behavior for the SIM runtime: async, backtracking, conditions.

The kernel defines the control-policy contracts; this crate supplies the concrete control organ (coroutines, generators, restarts, non-local exits) layered over those contracts.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Async](https://docs.rs/struct.AsyncTask.html)- Task
- A deterministic async task that resolves after a fixed number of polls.
- [Backtracker](https://docs.rs/struct.Backtracker.html)
- A linear backtracking choice point over a fixed list of alternatives.
- [Condition](https://docs.rs/struct.Condition.html)
- A signalled condition: a kind symbol plus a payload reference.
- [Condition](https://docs.rs/struct.ConditionHandler.html)- Handler
- A handler bound to a condition kind, prompt, and capture continuation.
- [Condition](https://docs.rs/struct.ConditionStack.html)- Stack
- A stack of `ConditionHandler`
- [Continuation](https://docs.rs/struct.ContinuationValue.html)- Value
- A runtime object wrapping a captured continuation and its capture result.
- [Control](https://docs.rs/struct.ControlFunction.html)- Function
- A callable runtime object exposing one control primitive.
- [Control](https://docs.rs/struct.ControlLib.html)- Lib
- The control organ as a loadable kernel `Lib`
- [Control](https://docs.rs/struct.ControlResultValue.html)- Result - Value
- A runtime object wrapping the result reference of a control operation.
- [Control](https://docs.rs/struct.ControlTag.html)- Tag
- Stable tag identifying a delimited control prompt.
- [Coroutine](https://docs.rs/struct.Coroutine.html)
- Two cooperating value streams that yield by alternating between lanes.
- [Generator](https://docs.rs/struct.Generator.html)
- A single-lane generator that yields a fixed sequence of values on demand.
- [Labeled](https://docs.rs/struct.LabeledPrompt.html)- Prompt
- A labeled escape target: a label symbol bound to a control prompt.
- [NonLocal](https://docs.rs/struct.NonLocalExit.html)- Exit
- A pending non-local exit: a kind, a target label, and a carried value.
- [OneShot](https://docs.rs/struct.OneShotControlPolicy.html)- Control - Policy
- A control policy that allows each captured continuation to resume once.
- [Restart](https://docs.rs/struct.Restart.html)
- A named recovery point: a symbol bound to a captured continuation.
- [Restart](https://docs.rs/struct.RestartStack.html)- Stack
- A stack of `Restart`
- [Segmented](https://docs.rs/struct.SegmentedControlPolicy.html)- Control - Policy
- A one-shot control policy scoped to a named delimited segment.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Async](https://docs.rs/enum.AsyncPoll.html)- Poll
- Outcome of polling an `AsyncTask`
- [Backtrack](https://docs.rs/enum.BacktrackStep.html)- Step
- Result of advancing a `Backtracker`
- [Coroutine](https://docs.rs/enum.CoroutineLane.html)- Lane
- Identifies which of a coroutine’s two cooperating lanes yielded a value.
- [Coroutine](https://docs.rs/enum.CoroutineStep.html)- Step
- Outcome of resuming a `Coroutine`
- [Generator](https://docs.rs/enum.GeneratorStep.html)- Step
- Outcome of advancing a `Generator`
- [NonLocal](https://docs.rs/enum.NonLocalExitKind.html)- Exit - Kind
- The flavor of a non-local exit: loop break, loop continue, or block return.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Control](https://docs.rs/trait.ControlPrompt.html)- Prompt
- Library-level contract for prompts raised by runtime organs.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [abort_](https://docs.rs/fn.abort_symbol.html)- symbol
- Returns the `control/abort`symbol.
- [capture_](https://docs.rs/fn.capture_symbol.html)- symbol
- Returns the `control/capture`symbol.

`prompt`,`capture`,`abort`, and`resume`.
- [control_](https://docs.rs/fn.control_organ_symbol.html)- organ_ - symbol
- Returns the `organ/control`symbol identifying this control organ.
- [escape_](https://docs.rs/fn.escape_to_label.html)- to_ - label
- Performs `exit`by aborting to the matching`LabeledPrompt``prompts`.
- [install_](https://docs.rs/fn.install_control_lib.html)- control_ - lib
- Installs the control organ into `cx`: loads`ControlLib`
- [install_](https://docs.rs/fn.install_control_policy.html)- control_ - policy
- Installs the default `one_shot_control_policy``cx`as the active control policy.

- Invokes the restart named `name`on`stack`with`value`; free-function form of`RestartStack::invoke`

- Builds a shared `OneShotControlPolicy``ControlPolicyRef`

- Returns the `control/prompt`symbol.
- [publish_](https://docs.rs/fn.publish_control_organ_claims.html)- control_ - organ_ - claims
- Publishes the control organ’s claims into `cx`, recording that this organ supplies the standard`control_op_keys``control_organ_symbol`
- [publish_](https://docs.rs/fn.publish_control_organ_claims_for_lib.html)- control_ - organ_ - claims_ - for_ - lib
- Publishes control organ claims as part of a loaded lib receipt.
- [raise_](https://docs.rs/fn.raise_prompt.html)- prompt
- Raises a library-level control prompt through the kernel control contract.
- [resume_](https://docs.rs/fn.resume_symbol.html)- symbol
- Returns the `control/resume`symbol.
- [segmented_](https://docs.rs/fn.segmented_control_policy.html)- control_ - policy

- [signal_](https://docs.rs/fn.signal_condition.html)- condition

# sim_value - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-value/^0.1.0-rc.1/

## Expand description

Ergonomic construction and access for kernel `Expr` data.

The kernel `Expr` enum is bare data with no ergonomic surface, so dozens of
libs independently re-grew `sym`/`number`/`field`/`set`/`expr_kind` and a
`k`/`i` path-addressing scheme. This crate is the one home for that. It
depends only on `sim-kernel` and adds data ergonomics, not runtime behavior,
so it does not touch the kernel boundary.

- `build`- `sym`,- `int`,- `float`,- `text`,- `list`,- `map`, …);
- `access`- `field`,- `set`,- `remove`, …);
- `kind`- `Expr`variant classifier (- `expr_kind`);
- `path`- `Path`,- `get`,- `set_at`).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use sim_value::access::{field, set};
use sim_value::build::{int, map, sym};
let value = map(vec![("a", int(1)), ("b", int(2))]);
assert_eq!(field(&value, "a"), Some(&int(1)));
let updated = set(&value, "a", int(9));
assert_eq!(field(&updated, "a"), Some(&int(9)));
assert_eq!(field(&updated, "b"), Some(&int(2))); // siblings preserved
let _ = sym("ok");
```

---

# sim_lib_lang_clojure - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sim-lib-lang-clojure/0.1.0-rc.1/target-redirect/sim_lib_lang_clojure/

Clojure surface profile for the SIM runtime.

# sim_lib_lang_clojure - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-lang-clojure/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_lang_clojure/index.html

## Expand description

Clojure surface profile for the SIM runtime.

The kernel defines the codec, eval-policy, and `Expr` contracts; this crate
is a loadable language profile presenting a Clojure/EDN surface syntax over
the shared `Expr` graph, not a standalone interpreter.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Clojure](https://docs.rs/struct.ClojureEdnCodec.html)- EdnCodec
- Decoder that reads Clojure/EDN surface syntax into the shared `Expr`
- [Clojure](https://docs.rs/struct.ClojureEdnCodecLib.html)- EdnCodec - Lib
- Loadable `Lib``ClojureEdnCodec`

# ClojureEdnCodec in sim_lib_lang_clojure - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-lang-clojure/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_lang_clojure/struct.ClojureEdnCodec.html

`pub struct ClojureEdnCodec;`## Expand description

Decoder that reads Clojure/EDN surface syntax into the shared [ Expr](https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_kernel/expr/enum.Expr.html) graph.

Implements the kernel [ Decoder](https://docs.rs/sim-codec/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_codec/implementation/runtime/trait.Decoder.html),

[, and](https://docs.rs/sim-codec/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_codec/implementation/runtime/trait.LocatedDecoder.html)

`LocatedDecoder`[contracts; this profile only decodes (surface ->](https://docs.rs/sim-codec/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_codec/implementation/runtime/trait.TreeDecoder.html)

`TreeDecoder``Expr`) and registers no
encoder. See the [crate](https://docs.rs/index.html)README for the language-profile role.

        expr: [Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<[Expr](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html)>,
        annotations: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<([Symbol](https://docs.rs/id/struct.Symbol.html), [Expr](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html))>,
    },
    Extension {
        tag: [Symbol](https://docs.rs/id/struct.Symbol.html),
        payload: [Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<[Expr](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html)>,
    },
}## Expand description

The codec-neutral expression graph: the checked form of source.

The kernel defines this graph; general-purpose codecs in library crates
round-trip every expression through it. It is the `checked forms` stage of
the data flow `tokens -> checked forms -> objects -> checked calls -> objects -> encoded forms`. Equality and hashing are canonical (see
[ Expr::canonical_eq](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html#method.canonical_eq)): map entries and set members compare order-insensitively.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
let call = Expr::Call {
    operator: Box::new(Expr::Symbol(Symbol::new("add"))),
    args: vec![Expr::Bool(true), Expr::Nil],
};
// Maps compare canonically regardless of entry order.
let a = Expr::Set(vec![Expr::Bool(true), Expr::Nil]);
let b = Expr::Set(vec![Expr::Nil, Expr::Bool(true)]);
assert!(a.canonical_eq(&b));
let _ = call;
```

# ClojureEdnCodecLib in sim_lib_lang_clojure - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-lang-clojure/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_lang_clojure/struct.ClojureEdnCodecLib.html

`pub struct ClojureEdnCodecLib { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Loadable [ Lib](https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_kernel/library/loaders/trait.Lib.html) that registers the

[as a runtime codec object.](https://docs.rs/struct.ClojureEdnCodec.html)

`ClojureEdnCodec`Exports a single [ Export::Codec](https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_kernel/library/model/enum.Export.html#variant.Codec) under

[and installs it via the](https://docs.rs/fn.clojure_edn_reader_symbol.html)

`clojure_edn_reader_symbol`[when loaded.](https://docs.rs/sim-kernel/0.1.0-rc.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sim_kernel/library/transaction/struct.Linker.html)

`Linker`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Load the codec and decode a small EDN form into the shared `Expr` graph:

```
use std::sync::Arc;
use sim_codec::{Input, decode_tree_with_codec};
use sim_kernel::{
    CapabilitySet, Cx, DefaultFactory, Expr, NoopEvalPolicy, ReadPolicy, TrustLevel,
};
use sim_lib_lang_clojure::{ClojureEdnCodecLib, clojure_edn_reader_symbol};
let mut cx = Cx::new(Arc::new(NoopEvalPolicy), Arc::new(DefaultFactory));
let codec_id = cx.registry_mut().fresh_codec_id();
cx.load_lib(&ClojureEdnCodecLib::new(codec_id))?;
let policy = ReadPolicy {
    trust: TrustLevel::TrustedSource,
    capabilities: CapabilitySet::new(),
};
let tree = decode_tree_with_codec(
    &mut cx,
    &clojure_edn_reader_symbol(),
    Input::Text("[1 2 3]".to_owned()),
    policy,
    "doc.edn",
)?;
assert!(matches!(tree.expr, Expr::Vector(_)));
```

# Value in sim_kernel::value - Rust

`pub struct Value(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

The universal runtime handle for every object.

A [ Value](https://docs.rs/struct.Value.html) is a reference-counted handle to a

[; it is the object end of the data flow](https://docs.rs/trait.RuntimeObject.html)

`RuntimeObject``tokens -> checked forms -> objects -> checked calls -> objects -> encoded forms`. Equality and hashing are by object
identity (pointer), not by structural contents.[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
// Every value exposes its object and that object's header.
let header = value.header();
let _same = value.object().header();
let _ = header;
```

# getrandom - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/getrandom/^0.2/

## Expand description

Interface to the operating system’s random number generator.

[§](https://docs.rs#supported-targets)Supported targets

| Target | Target Triple | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| Linux, Android | `*‑linux‑*` | system call if available, otherwise`getrandom`after successfully polling`/dev/urandom``/dev/random` |
| Windows | `*‑windows‑*` | `BCryptGenRandom` |
| macOS | `*‑apple‑darwin` | `getentropy` |
| iOS, tvOS, watchOS | `*‑apple‑ios`,`*-apple-tvos`,`*-apple-watchos` | `CCRandomGenerateBytes` |
| FreeBSD | `*‑freebsd` | `getrandom` |
| OpenBSD | `*‑openbsd` | `getentropy` |
| NetBSD | `*‑netbsd` | if available, otherwise`getrandom``kern.arandom` |
| Dragonfly BSD | `*‑dragonfly` | `getrandom` |
| Solaris | `*‑solaris` | (with`getrandom``GRND_RANDOM`) |
| illumos | `*‑illumos` | `getrandom` |
| Fuchsia OS | `*‑fuchsia` | `cprng_draw` |
| Redox | `*‑redox` | `/dev/urandom` |
| Haiku | `*‑haiku` | `/dev/urandom`(identical to`/dev/random`) |
| Hermit | `*-hermit` | `sys_read_entropy` |
| Hurd | `*-hurd-*` | `getrandom` |
| SGX | `x86_64‑*‑sgx` | `RDRAND` |
| VxWorks | `*‑wrs‑vxworks‑*` | `randABytes`after checking entropy pool initialization with`randSecure` |
| ESP-IDF | `*‑espidf` | `esp_fill_random` |
| Emscripten | `*‑emscripten` | `getentropy` |
| WASI | `wasm32‑wasi` | `random_get` |
| Web Browser and Node.js | `wasm*‑*‑unknown` | if available, then`Crypto.getRandomValues`if on Node.js, see`crypto.randomFillSync`[WebAssembly support](https://docs.rs#webassembly-support) |
| SOLID | `*-kmc-solid_*` | `SOLID_RNG_SampleRandomBytes` |
| Nintendo 3DS | `*-nintendo-3ds` | `getrandom` |
| PS Vita | `*-vita-*` | `getentropy` |
| QNX Neutrino | `*‑nto-qnx*` | (identical to`/dev/urandom``/dev/random`) |
| AIX | `*-ibm-aix` | `/dev/urandom` |
| Cygwin | `*-cygwin` | (based on`getrandom`)`RtlGenRandom` |

Pull Requests that add support for new targets to `getrandom` are always welcome.

[§](https://docs.rs#unsupported-targets)Unsupported targets

By default, `getrandom` will not compile on unsupported targets, but certain
features allow a user to select a “fallback” implementation if no supported
implementation exists.

All of the below mechanisms only affect unsupported
targets. Supported targets will *always* use their supported implementations.
This prevents a crate from overriding a secure source of randomness
(either accidentally or intentionally).

[§](https://docs.rs#devurandom-fallback-on-linux-and-android)`/dev/urandom` fallback on Linux and Android

On Linux targets the fallback is present only if either `target_env` is `musl`,
or `target_arch` is one of the following: `aarch64`, `arm`, `powerpc`, `powerpc64`,
`s390x`, `x86`, `x86_64`. Other supported targets [require](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/rustc/platform-support.html)
kernel versions which support `getrandom` system call, so fallback is not needed.

On Android targets the fallback is present only for the following `target_arch`es:
`aarch64`, `arm`, `x86`, `x86_64`. Other `target_arch`es (e.g. RISC-V) require
sufficiently high API levels.

The fallback can be disabled by enabling the `linux_disable_fallback` crate feature.
Note that doing so will bump minimum supported Linux kernel version to 3.17 and
Android API level to 23 (Marshmallow).

[§](https://docs.rs#rdrand-on-x86)RDRAND on x86

*If the  rdrand Cargo feature is enabled*,

`getrandom` will fallback to using
the [instruction to get randomness on](https://software.intel.com/en-us/articles/intel-digital-random-number-generator-drng-software-implementation-guide)

`RDRAND``no_std` `x86`/`x86_64`
targets. This feature has no effect on other CPU architectures.[§](https://docs.rs#webassembly-support)WebAssembly support

This crate fully supports the
[ wasm32-wasi](https://github.com/CraneStation/wasi) and

[targets. However, the](https://www.hellorust.com/setup/emscripten/)

`wasm32-unknown-emscripten``wasm32-unknown-unknown` target (i.e. the target used
by `wasm-pack`) is not automatically
supported since, from the target name alone, we cannot deduce which
JavaScript interface is in use (or if JavaScript is available at all).Instead, *if the  js Cargo feature is enabled*, this crate will assume
that you are building for an environment containing JavaScript, and will
call the appropriate methods. Both web browser (main window and Web Workers)
and Node.js environments are supported, invoking the methods

[described above](https://docs.rs#supported-targets)using the

[toolchain.](https://github.com/rustwasm/wasm-bindgen)

`wasm-bindgen`To enable the `js` Cargo feature, add the following to the `dependencies`
section in your `Cargo.toml` file:

```
[dependencies]
getrandom = { version = "0.2", features = ["js"] }
```
This can be done even if `getrandom` is not a direct dependency. Cargo
allows crates to enable features for indirect dependencies.

This feature should only be enabled for binary, test, or benchmark crates.
Library crates should generally not enable this feature, leaving such a
decision to *users* of their library. Also, libraries should not introduce
their own `js` features *just* to enable `getrandom`’s `js` feature.

This feature has no effect on targets other than `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

[§](https://docs.rs#nodejs-es-module-support)Node.js ES module support

Node.js supports both [CommonJS modules](https://nodejs.org/api/modules.html) and [ES modules](https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html). Due to
limitations in wasm-bindgen’s [ module](https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-bindgen/reference/attributes/on-js-imports/module.html) support, we cannot directly
support ES Modules running on Node.js. However, on Node v15 and later, the
module author can add a simple shim to support the Web Cryptography API:

```
import { webcrypto } from 'node:crypto'
globalThis.crypto = webcrypto
```
This crate will then use the provided `webcrypto` implementation.

[§](https://docs.rs#platform-support)Platform Support

This crate generally supports the same operating system and platform versions that the Rust standard library does. Additional targets may be supported using pluggable custom implementations.

This means that as Rust drops support for old versions of operating systems
(such as old Linux kernel versions, Android API levels, etc) in stable releases,
`getrandom` may create new patch releases (`0.N.x`) that remove support for
outdated platform versions.

[§](https://docs.rs#custom-implementations)Custom implementations

The [ register_custom_getrandom!](https://docs.rs/macro.register_custom_getrandom.html) macro allows a user to mark their own
function as the backing implementation for

[. See the macro’s documentation for more information about writing and registering your own custom implementations.](https://docs.rs/fn.getrandom.html)

`getrandom`Note that registering a custom implementation only has an effect on targets
that would otherwise not compile. Any supported targets (including those
using `rdrand` and `js` Cargo features) continue using their normal
implementations even if a function is registered.

[§](https://docs.rs#early-boot)Early boot

Sometimes, early in the boot process, the OS has not collected enough entropy to securely seed its RNG. This is especially common on virtual machines, where standard “random” events are hard to come by.

Some operating system interfaces always block until the RNG is securely seeded. This can take anywhere from a few seconds to more than a minute. A few (Linux, NetBSD and Solaris) offer a choice between blocking and getting an error; in these cases, we always choose to block.

On Linux (when the `getrandom` system call is not available), reading from
`/dev/urandom` never blocks, even when the OS hasn’t collected enough
entropy yet. To avoid returning low-entropy bytes, we first poll
`/dev/random` and only switch to `/dev/urandom` once this has succeeded.

On OpenBSD, this kind of entropy accounting isn’t available, and on NetBSD, blocking on it is discouraged. On these platforms, nonblocking interfaces are used, even when reliable entropy may not be available. On the platforms where it is used, the reliability of entropy accounting itself isn’t free from controversy. This library provides randomness sourced according to the platform’s best practices, but each platform has its own limits on the grade of randomness it can promise in environments with few sources of entropy.

[§](https://docs.rs#error-handling)Error handling

We always choose failure over returning known insecure “random” bytes. In
general, on supported platforms, failure is highly unlikely, though not
impossible. If an error does occur, then it is likely that it will occur
on every call to `getrandom`, hence after the first successful call one
can be reasonably confident that no errors will occur.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [register_](https://docs.rs/macro.register_custom_getrandom.html)- custom_ - getrandom
- Register a function to be invoked by `getrandom`on unsupported targets.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- A small and `no_std`compatible error type

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [getrandom](https://docs.rs/fn.getrandom.html)
- Fill `dest`with random bytes from the system’s preferred random number source.
- [getrandom_](https://docs.rs/fn.getrandom_uninit.html)- uninit
- Version of the `getrandom`function which fills`dest`with random bytes returns a mutable reference to those bytes.

# prikk_crypto - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/prikk-crypto/^0/

## Expand description

Prikk cryptographic primitives.

v1 scope is intentionally minimal: Ed25519 keypair construction, detached signing, and detached verification. Trust stores, key persistence, key rotation, revocation, and signature policy are out of scope here and belong to later phases (RFC-025). This crate is the single home for the v1 signing/verification algorithm so authoring, sealing, and verification cannot diverge.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Ed25519](https://docs.rs/struct.Ed25519KeyPair.html)- KeyPair
- An Ed25519 keypair used to produce detached signatures.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [ED25519_](https://docs.rs/constant.ED25519_KEY_LEN.html)- KEY_ - LEN
- Length in bytes of an Ed25519 secret seed and of an Ed25519 public key.
- [ED25519_](https://docs.rs/constant.ED25519_SIGNATURE_LEN.html)- SIGNATURE_ - LEN
- Length in bytes of an Ed25519 detached signature.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [verify_](https://docs.rs/fn.verify_ed25519.html)- ed25519
- Verify a detached Ed25519 `signature`over`message`against a 32-byte`public_key`.

# prikk_error - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/prikk-error/^0/

## Expand description

Shared error taxonomy for Prikk crates.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- Error type used by the initial implementation crates.

# prikk_hash - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/prikk-hash/^0/

## Expand description

Hash primitives used by Prikk.

This crate intentionally contains a tiny first-party SHA-256 implementation for the initial source drop so the object identity path does not depend on external crates. A later RFC-backed decision may replace this with an audited dependency if the release policy prefers that.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Sha256](https://docs.rs/type.Sha256Digest.html)- Digest
- A 32-byte SHA-256 digest.

---

# prikk_object - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/prikk-object/^0/

## Expand description

Object identity and canonical payload definitions for Prikk.

This crate deliberately does **not** use protobuf bytes for object identity. It implements a
small deterministic canonical encoder seed that can be extended as FDD-03 matures.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use canonical::`- [CanonicalEncode](https://docs.rs/canonical/trait.CanonicalEncode.html);
- `pub use canonical::`- [CanonicalWriter](https://docs.rs/canonical/struct.CanonicalWriter.html);
- `pub use canonical::`- [WireType](https://docs.rs/canonical/enum.WireType.html);
- `pub use envelope::`- [ObjectEnvelope](https://docs.rs/envelope/struct.ObjectEnvelope.html);
- `pub use id::`- [OBJECT_ID_DOMAIN](https://docs.rs/id/constant.OBJECT_ID_DOMAIN.html);
- `pub use id::`- [ObjectId](https://docs.rs/id/struct.ObjectId.html);
- `pub use id::`- [ObjectType](https://docs.rs/id/enum.ObjectType.html);
- `pub use signature::`- [Signature](https://docs.rs/signature/struct.Signature.html);
- `pub use signature::`- [SignatureAlgorithm](https://docs.rs/signature/enum.SignatureAlgorithm.html);
- `pub use signature::`- [SignerRole](https://docs.rs/signature/enum.SignerRole.html);
- `pub use`- [payload](https://docs.rs/payload/index.html)::*;
